tools.title: Behavior Trees & Blackboards
tools.summary: Event-driven decision trees backed by Blackboard state for scalable NPC behavior.
workflow: Use Services sparingly for periodic updates.
Debug with the live Behavior Tree and Gameplay Debugger.
tools.codex: Codex can author Tasks/Services and review graph complexity; future MCP readers should expose tree nodes and Blackboard keys.
tools.caution: Do not turn the Blackboard into a global dumping ground or run expensive Services every tick.

tools.title: Environment Query System (EQS)
tools.summary: Scores generated locations or actors against tests so AI can choose cover, vantage points, pickups and other context-sensitive targets.
workflow: Create a focused query with a small candidate set.
Use EQS debugging visualization and profile expensive tests.
tools.codex: Useful for replacing hand-written nearest/cover search loops with an engine-native query asset.
tools.caution: Large generators and expensive traces can become a hidden AI performance cost.

tools.title: AI Perception
tools.summary: Sensory framework for sight, hearing, damage and custom stimuli that feeds AI awareness.
workflow: Add AI Perception to the controller.
Store semantic state rather than re-querying perception everywhere.
tools.codex: Codex should prefer perception events over ad-hoc distance checks on Tick for awareness systems.
tools.caution: Tune sight/hearing ranges and affiliation filters; uncontrolled perception across many agents can be expensive.

tools.title: Smart Objects
tools.summary: Reservation-based world interaction points that advertise activities to AI and players.
why: Decouples world interactions from specific NPC classes
Scales benches, doors, workstations and ambient behaviors
workflow: Release the slot reliably on completion/cancel.
tools.codex: Good architecture for systemic NPC/environment interactions instead of casts to every interactable class.
tools.caution: Always handle cancellation and reservation release; orphaned claims create hard-to-debug AI stalls.

tools.title: World Partition
tools.summary: Grid-based automatic level streaming and large-world data management with OFPA, Data Layers and builder commandlets.
workflow: Define streaming sources and data layers.
Use builder commandlets for batch work.
Profile streaming and memory on target hardware.
tools.codex: Codex can maintain world-partition config and invoke builder commandlets, but should not bulk-resave a world without a clean branch and validation.
tools.caution: Streaming grids and cross-cell references need architectural discipline; do not enable merely because the project uses UE5.

tools.title: World Partition HLOD
tools.summary: Generates proxy representations for unloaded World Partition cells to reduce draw calls while preserving distant scenery.
workflow: Create HLOD layers by content type.
Run full HLOD builder in CI/release pipelines.
Validate visual transitions and package size.
tools.codex: A strong candidate for project scripts that build only changed/target regions and report failures.
tools.caution: HLOD generation can create many binary changes; coordinate source control and avoid unnecessary full rebuilds.

tools.title: Rewind Debugger
tools.summary: Records PIE gameplay and lets developers scrub backward through animation/gameplay traces to inspect what actually happened.
workflow: Pause and select the target object.
tools.codex: Use trace findings as evidence when Codex edits animation logic instead of describing the bug from memory.
tools.caution: Enable Pose Watch/trace data intentionally; recording everything can add overhead and noise.

tools.title: Animation Insights
tools.summary: Unreal Insights extension for observing animation state, blend values and animation performance over recorded traces.
tools.codex: Provide Codex with the measured track/state evidence before refactoring complex animation systems.
tools.caution: Profile representative gameplay; editor preview behavior may not match a packaged target exactly.

tools.title: Control Rig
tools.summary: In-engine rigging and procedural animation framework usable from Sequencer, Animation Blueprints and gameplay Blueprints.
why: Rig and adjust characters without round-tripping every change to a DCC
Full Body IK and modular rig workflows
workflow: Create a Control Rig from the skeletal mesh.
Use it in Sequencer or Anim Blueprints where appropriate.
Use Rewind/Animation Insights for runtime diagnosis.
tools.codex: Useful target for future graph extraction/authoring support and for generating project-specific procedural rig utilities.
tools.caution: Separate rig authoring from gameplay state ownership; complex per-frame rigs can be costly.

tools.title: Motion Warping
tools.summary: Dynamically adjusts root motion to align animation windows with named world targets for mantling, melee, traversal and interactions.
why: Reuse animations across variable target positions
Avoids bespoke animations for every distance
workflow: Set/update named warp targets before playback.
Test edge distances/rotations and network behavior.
tools.codex: Codex can build consistent traversal/melee wrappers around warp targets instead of hard-coded teleport corrections.
tools.caution: Beta feature; validate root-motion, prediction and multiplayer behavior on the exact target engine/build.

tools.title: Motion Matching / Pose Search
tools.summary: Query-driven pose selection from animation databases as an alternative to large hand-authored locomotion state machines.
why: Scales by adding quality animation data
workflow: Define a schema and pose database.
Tune cost weights with representative gameplay.
Profile database/query cost and debug selections.
tools.codex: Use as a deliberate animation architecture, not an automatic replacement for every state machine.
tools.caution: Quality depends heavily on animation coverage/data preparation; a sparse database will not be rescued by code.

tools.title: Niagara VFX
tools.summary: Unreal's modern programmable VFX system for reusable CPU/GPU particle and simulation effects.
workflow: Build reusable modules before giant one-off graphs.
Expose user parameters for gameplay control.
Profile with Niagara Debugger on target scenarios.
tools.codex: Node2Code can help with read context today; future native MCP tools should inspect/author Niagara graphs directly.
tools.caution: VFX can silently consume GPU/CPU/memory; define effect budgets and scalability levels early.

tools.title: Niagara Debugger
tools.summary: Live level-wide inspection and performance analysis for Niagara systems, emitters and parameters.
why: Faster VFX debugging than graph inspection alone
tools.codex: Use debugger output as objective evidence before asking Codex to optimize Niagara content.
tools.caution: Optimize representative scenes; isolated editor previews can hide aggregate VFX cost.

tools.title: MetaSounds
tools.summary: Sample-accurate DSP graph system for procedural, interactive and reusable audio sources.
why: Procedural audio without external middleware for many cases
workflow: Create reusable Patches for shared DSP logic.
Profile render cost and voice counts.
Keep gameplay events and audio rendering responsibilities separate.
tools.codex: Strong future MCP graph target; today Codex can help design parameter contracts and Builder API utilities.
tools.caution: Audio graphs are DSP flow graphs, not Blueprint execution graphs; reason about real-time audio constraints.

tools.title: MetaSound Builder API
tools.summary: Blueprint/C++ API for procedurally creating and modifying MetaSound Sources/Patches and graph connections.
why: Can create assets from Editor Utility Blueprints
Excellent candidate for Codex-native audio tooling
workflow: Use the Builder subsystem for in-memory/runtime generation.
Use the Editor subsystem for asset authoring.
Wrap repetitive project patterns in deterministic helpers.
Verify documented unsupported graph features before relying on them.
tools.codex: This is the preferred engine-native foundation for future MetaSound MCP tools instead of UI automation.
tools.caution: The API is Beta and has documented limitations; pin to UE 5.8 and smoke-test after engine upgrades.

tools.title: RenderDoc Integration
tools.summary: Single-frame GPU graphics capture integrated into Unreal for inspecting draw events, resources, pipeline state and shaders.
workflow: Install RenderDoc and enable/attach the Unreal plugin.
Fix and capture the same scenario again.
tools.codex: Provide capture findings/event names to Codex for targeted rendering changes; do not ask it to optimize blindly from FPS alone.
tools.caution: Full-resource/callstack captures can become very large and profiling itself adds overhead.

tools.title: Render Resource Viewer
tools.summary: Snapshot of GPU memory allocations with resource size, flags, owner asset and filtering/search.
workflow: Open the viewer in the representative scene.
Browse large allocations to the owning asset.
tools.codex: Future MCP export could rank resource owners automatically; for now use the viewer to supply measured asset targets.
tools.caution: It is a snapshot, not continuous tracing; refresh after state changes.

tools.title: Iris Replication System
tools.summary: Opt-in next-generation replication system designed for larger worlds/player counts with shared work, filtering and prioritization.
why: Existing replicated properties/RPCs remain largely compatible
workflow: First build correct authoritative gameplay with normal replication.
Evaluate Iris on a dedicated branch.
tools.codex: Codex must not flip a project to Iris as a casual optimization; migration needs architecture review and measured validation.
tools.caution: Epic marks Iris Experimental in UE 5.8; use caution for shipping and verify all project-specific replication behaviors.

tools.title: Replication Graph
tools.summary: Persistent replication-list graph that scales server relevancy work for large numbers of Actors and clients.
why: Good bridge when generic replication becomes CPU-bound
workflow: Create focused custom nodes only where needed.
tools.codex: Use only after profiling shows replication-list generation is a bottleneck; Codex can help implement/test custom nodes.
tools.caution: Adds networking architecture complexity and the plugin is marked Beta; splitscreen limitations are documented.

tools.title: Crash Reporter + Crash Context
tools.summary: Captures crash IDs, call stacks, logs, system data and custom game context, with support for routing packaged-game reports to your own backend/service.
workflow: Include Crash Reporter in test/release packages.
Route reports to an approved service/backend.
Add compact custom context such as map/mode/build/session.
Triage recurring signatures and link fixes to build versions.
tools.codex: Codex can analyze symbolicated call stacks/logs and correlate them with source changes; never send secrets/PII as crash context.
tools.caution: Packaged builds need explicit Crash Reporter configuration; protect user privacy and keep symbols/build IDs organized.

tools.title: Structured Unreal Logging Strategy
tools.summary: Use project-specific log categories, appropriate verbosity and structured UE_LOGFMT messages so bugs are searchable instead of buried in LogTemp spam.
why: Structured fields are easier for Codex to interpret
workflow: Create one category per meaningful subsystem/domain.
Use Error/Warning only for actionable problems.
Use Log/Verbose for normal diagnostic detail.
Prefer UE_LOGFMT for structured messages where useful.
Allow verbosity overrides via -LogCmds during debugging.
tools.codex: Logs should include stable identifiers/state needed for diagnosis; Codex can then search logs deterministically without parsing arbitrary on-screen text.
tools.caution: Never log secrets/tokens/PII, and avoid per-frame spam in normal verbosity levels.
